title: Powertoys Dock not populating after update, w10 x64, top, always-ontop

judgment.rationale: The reporter has now supplied the Command Palette settings, recent state, and bookmarks. The settings save Dock bands for the built-in Core and Bookmarks providers while both providers are disabled. Current CmdPal code removes disabled-provider dock bands and omits saved bands whose commands are unavailable, which plausibly explains the blank Dock. Confirming the effect of re-enabling those providers is more discriminating than asking for another archive.
evidence: The reporter says the Dock window appears and auto-hides but its system information and shortcuts are blank; drag/drop and the plus controls do not restore items.
The latest author comment at https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/50777#issuecomment-5902453453 attaches Command Palette settings.json, state.json, and bookmarks.json.
The attached settings include saved Dock bands for com.microsoft.cmdpal.builtin.core and Bookmarks, while ProviderSettings marks both providers disabled.

At upstream commit 31bf904826709b81b4a9bd9756788a0596f2ff81, TopLevelCommandManager.UpdateProviderEnabledStateAsyncCore removes dock bands for a disabled provider; DockViewModel.SetupBands omits saved bands when LookupDockBand cannot find the command.

Earlier PowerToys diagnostics and a general PowerToys settings file were also supplied, but maintainers clarified that Command Palette has its own settings; the latest attachments now include those CmdPal files.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask the reporter to enable the Core and Bookmarks providers in Command Palette settings, restart Command Palette, and confirm whether the Dock content returns; do not request another diagnostic archive yet.

fix_assessment.rationale: The supplied settings currently point to expected disabled-provider behavior rather than a demonstrated code defect. No code fix is justified unless the reporter confirms the providers are enabled and the Dock remains blank.

issue_context.summary: The Dock is still blank after the reporter supplied its own Command Palette configuration. That configuration pins bands from providers currently marked disabled, and CmdPal's live band lookup omits unavailable commands.
known_information: The issue reports PowerToys 0.101.2373 Preview on Windows 10 x64.
The Dock appears and auto-hides, but the expected system-information and shortcut content is absent.
The reporter says the configured monitor did not change and attempted to add shortcuts through the Dock edit controls.
The latest attachments include Command Palette settings.json, state.json, and bookmarks.json.
The supplied settings save Dock bands for the built-in Core and Bookmarks providers while their ProviderSettings entries have IsEnabled=false.
inferences: The disabled provider settings may explain why the saved bands are not available to the Dock after startup.
The settings do not establish why the providers became disabled or whether enabling them will restore the expected system-information and shortcut content.
issue_context.analysis: The direct configuration/code correspondence is a stronger lead than the earlier general PowerToys settings file. The current implementation removes dock-band items when a provider is disabled and reconstructs visible bands only from commands that are loaded. The smallest useful next step is to enable the two referenced providers and confirm whether the symptom clears.
initial_investigation: Read all 17 live comments, including the latest three CmdPal attachment links.

Inspected TopLevelCommandManager.UpdateProviderEnabledStateAsyncCore, DockViewModel.SetupBands, and the reporter's saved provider/band state at upstream commit 31bf904826709b81b4a9bd9756788a0596f2ff81.

information_gaps.why_needed: This distinguishes the currently visible disabled-provider configuration from an independent Dock initialization or update regression.

comment.body: Thanks for adding the Command Palette settings, state, and bookmarks files. The settings save Dock bands for the built-in Core and Bookmarks providers, but both providers are currently marked disabled. In CmdPal, disabling a provider removes its Dock bands, so this may explain why the saved items are not appearing. Please enable Core and Bookmarks in Command Palette settings, restart Command Palette, and confirm whether the system-information and shortcut bands return. This will distinguish the saved provider state from a separate Dock update/initialization problem. No additional diagnostics or configuration export are needed for this check.
